chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
One does not sit between As-Safa and Al-Marwa except due to tiredness.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa (the first hill in the Sa'i ritual)
key_terms.وَالْمَرْوَةِ: And Al-Marwa (the second hill in the Sa'i ritual)

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to sit between Safa and Marwa during Sa'i?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juristic distinction between permissible resting due to physical exertion (jahd) and prohibited leisurely sitting during Sa'i, reflecting the Shia emphasis on preserving the ritual's spiritual intensity. This ruling is often discussed in fiqh manuals alongside the permissibility of riding for the elderly or weak, highlighting the balance between ease and reverence in Hajj rituals. The prohibition underscores that Sa'i is an act of worship requiring active engagement, not merely a transit between landmarks.
